audit.why: Exactly 50.0% over 240 games against a chart that gives Camille levels 1-5 and first item, calls 6 a Skill stage, and hands Maokai the two-item attrition game. A dead-even headline number produced by an early lead that decays into a tank is coherent, so no stage moved.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike is keyed to 'his W cooldown' with no number, and Nature's Grasp (R) does not appear anywhere in the matchup - so the level-6 stage is written as if his ult does not exist.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10s, Bramble Smash 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, Sapling Toss 18/17/16/15/14s, Nature's Grasp 130/110/90s. The 14s on his W at rank 1 is the window every dive on this page depends on and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, spikes[2].text, early, mid and wants.you[2] now carry the 14s W window, and spikes[1] names Nature's Grasp as the rooting wall he owns at 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The interaction that wastes your whole combo is absent: Twisted Advance makes Maokai UNTARGETABLE while it travels. The page says only that it 'cancels your E mid-flight', so a player dumps Q-recast and R into a target that cannot be hit. Sap Magic's cooldown is also reduced every time he casts a spell or is struck by one - meaning your own poke speeds up his heal - and there is no Grievous Wounds call anywhere. Camille's Hookshot is called a stun; Riot's text says knock-up.
audit.why: Riot, Twisted Advance: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target. Upon arrival, he roots the target.' Sap Magic: 'Each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an enemy's spell, this cooldown is reduced.' _missing-interactions.json flags untargetable-dodges-burst for this pairing.
audit.corrected: early, mid, wants.you[0] and whys[4] now say wait the dash out rather than spending into it, and mid buys anti-heal against a Sap Magic he refreshes off your own spells.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal timing, in a lane the page itself says he wins by out-healing your poke.
audit.why: Sap Magic is his whole attrition plan and it comes back faster the more spells fly, so Grievous Wounds bought before the two-item stage is the itemisation answer.
audit.corrected: mid now names the Grievous Wounds timing.

edits.before: Hextech Ultimatum cages him for a clean 1v1, but his Twisted Advance root and Bramble Smash knockback still interrupt your DPS inside the arena — hold E to dash OUT, not just in.
edits.after: Hextech Ultimatum cages him, but Nature's Grasp roots through your arena and Bramble Smash (7s) knocks you off your DPS — and Twisted Advance goes untargetable on the way in. Hold E to dash OUT.

edits.before: Sheen/bruiser item plus boots is your cleanest all-in: bait his W dash-root first, then E-stun on the cooldown when he can't yank himself onto you to cancel it.
edits.after: Sheen/bruiser item plus boots is your cleanest all-in: bait Twisted Advance first, then E in during the 14s it is down and he cannot yank himself onto you to cancel it.

edits.before: Bait his Twisted Advance root and Bramble Smash knockback, then E-stun in and Q-recast for the true-damage burst
edits.after: Wait out the untargetable Twisted Advance dash and Bramble Smash, then E in and Q-recast for the burst

edits.before: All-in on his W cooldown so he can't dash-root onto you and cancel your E mid-flight
edits.after: All-in during the 14s Twisted Advance is down so he can't dash-root onto you

edits.before: Your R isolates him but his W root and Q knockback can interrupt the DPS, so the all-in is a coin flip.
edits.after: Your R isolates him but Nature's Grasp and Bramble Smash knock you off the DPS, so the all-in is a coin flip.

edits.before: Maokai's W (Twisted Advance) is a targeted root that dashes HIM onto you and will cancel your E grapple mid-flight, so don't throw your engage while it's up — bait it first. At Level 1 his sapling poke and Sap Magic sustain out-value your single ability, so just last-hit and wait for your spike. His Q (Bramble Smash) knockback can also interrupt your Q-recast, so respect both before you commit.
edits.after: Maokai's W (Twisted Advance, 14s) is a targeted root that dashes HIM onto you, and he is UNTARGETABLE for the whole flight — burst spent into it is burst wasted, and it cancels your E grapple on arrival. Bait it first. At Level 1 his sapling poke and Sap Magic sustain out-value your single ability, so last-hit and wait. Bramble Smash (Q, 7s) knocks you out of your Q-recast window too.

edits.before: Levels 3 to 5 are your window: Q's recast hit deals true damage his armor can't soak, and W's outer edge chunks his max HP while healing you off him. Walk up behind your passive shield, trade in short bursts, and step away before saplings stack and Sap Magic heals it all back. At 6 your R isolates him for a 1v1, but his W root and Q knockback can still break the follow-up — keep E for the escape, not just the entry.
edits.after: Levels 3 to 5 are your window: Q's recast hit deals true damage his armor can't soak, and W's outer edge chunks his max HP while healing you off him. Buy Grievous Wounds early — Sap Magic's cooldown shortens every time a spell is cast or lands on him, so your own poke feeds his sustain. Trade in short bursts behind your passive shield. At 6 your R isolates him, but never dump the combo into an untargetable Twisted Advance — keep E for the escape.

edits.before: This is where he flips it. Maokai is a true tank — Sap Magic sustain, sapling zoning, and raw HP mean Tactical Sweep's percent damage stops mattering once he's itemized, and he simply doesn't die to your duel anymore. He out-sustains and out-front-lines you in extended fights, so use your tempo to take the map and isolate his carries with R instead of trying to kill him. Snowball before two items or this stalls into his favor.
edits.after: This is where he flips it. Maokai is a true tank — Sap Magic sustain that refreshes off every spell in the fight, sapling zoning, and raw HP mean Tactical Sweep's percent damage stops mattering once he's itemized, and he simply doesn't die to your duel anymore. He out-sustains and out-front-lines you, so use your tempo to take the map and isolate his carries with R instead of trying to kill him. Snowball before two items or this stalls into his favor.

edits.before: You own the bully window: bait W, E-stun in, Q-recast and W's edge while his sustain can't keep pace yet.
edits.after: You own the bully window: bait W, E knock-up in, Q-recast and W's edge while his sustain can't keep pace yet.

edits.before: Hookshot (E) unlocks your wall-dash stun and attack-speed burst. Only take a wall trade when Maokai's Twisted Advance is down, then peel out on the bonus move speed before he answers. Camille is favoured here.
edits.after: Hookshot (E) unlocks your wall-dash knock-up and attack-speed burst. Only take a wall trade when Maokai's Twisted Advance is down, then peel out on the bonus move speed before he answers. Camille is favoured here.

edits.before: Good trade: Lead with the W outer edge as Maokai steps to last-hit, weave the empowered Q2 true damage, then peel out on your bonus move speed before the fight goes long. Great trade: Maokai uses or whiffs Twisted Advance (Root): instantly E off a wall for the stun and attack-speed surge, Q-recast for the true-damage second hit, W to heal, and R to isolate him if he tries to run. Bad trade: Burning Hookshot (E) aggressively, missing the stun, and getting stuck in a drawn-out melee grind while your E and shield are down. That is how Camille loses a winning lane.

edits.before: Your E-stun off a wall into the empowered Q2 is a premium gank setup — ping your jungler when E is up and Maokai's escape is down. You are most vulnerable right after you E in with it on cooldown, so ward the river bush before you dive.

notes: The big one: Twisted Advance is untargetable for its entire flight, and the page only ever described it as something that cancels your E. A player who reads this file dumps Q-recast, W and R into a Maokai who cannot be hit, then finds himself rooted with everything on cooldown. Second: Sap Magic's cooldown is reduced by ANY spell cast or landing on him, so the poke pattern the page recommends actively accelerates his healing - that is the argument for early Grievous Wounds, which the matchup never made. Nature's Grasp did not appear in the content layer at all despite being the level-6 stage. I did not claim Bramble Smash grounds anything; maokai.json carries a grounding flag on it but Riot's text gives only a knock-back and a slow.
